statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-54787 (GHSA-wqqc-jjcq-vfxm): when sigstore-go verified a bundle signed with a self-managed long-lived key wrapped in its ExpiringKey type, it did not check the bundle's signing time against the key's validity window, so a bundle signed with expired key material could be accepted; deployments that use a certificate authority are not affected. It affects github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go up to and including 1.2.0 and is fixed in 1.2.1 by commit 4594ab4c (https://github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go/commit/4594ab4c779d08be1f4419803a8249188f35ed5f, 'Check signature time against public key validity window', pull request #642), which changes pkg/verify/signed_entity.go. Sources: https://github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go/security/advisories/GHSA-wqqc-jjcq-vfxm and https://github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go/releases/tag/v1.2.1. We checked every scout-sbom-indexer-dev package published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository as of 28 November 2026: 25 builds, 1.20.4-r1 to the current 1.30.0-r0, on x86_64 and aarch64 (50 packages), each against the checksum in the repository index. Each package holds one file, /sbom-indexer, a statically linked Go program for Linux built with CGO_ENABLED=0 (no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies). We read the program in full from every package, except 1.26.0-r3, whose program has the same SHA-1 checksum, recorded in its package header, as the 1.26.0-r2 program we read. The -dev program is built without the -w linker flag and without -trimpath; its Go release and module versions are the same as those of the scout-sbom-indexer program of the same build. Its Go build information, the same on both architectures, lists github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go v1.1.4 in 1.20.4-r1 to 1.23.1-r0, v1.2.0 in 1.23.1-r1, v1.2.1 in 1.23.1-r3 to 1.23.1-r10, v1.2.2 in 1.26.0-r1 to 1.30.0-r0, with no replace directive for that module. The v1.2.1 tag is the fix commit itself and v1.2.2 contains it (GitHub compare). The program does not compile in sigstore-go's verifier: reading the Go function table of every build, with runtime.main and sigstore-go's own pkg/bundle package initialiser (pkg/bundle.init) found in every build as controls, shows that the only sigstore-go functions linked are the package initialisers of pkg/bundle and pkg/verify, alongside their package-level variables. sigstore-go's (*Verifier).Verify in pkg/verify, the only non-test function the fix changes, is not linked in any build, no function from pkg/root, where ExpiringKey is defined, is linked, and no ValidAtTime method is linked. A byte search of every program, which also covers the source file names of inlined code, finds the path github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go/pkg/bundle (12 times in each) but neither github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go/pkg/root nor the source file name pkg/verify/signed_entity.go. Because the vulnerable code is not compiled into any published build, this package is not affected whatever sigstore-go version its build information lists. Debian marks its own sigstore-go source package no-dsa (minor issue) in trixie (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-54787); this decision does not rest on that, but on the absence of the code shown above.

We checked every scout-sbom-indexer-dev package published for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository as of 28 November 2026: 25 builds, 1.20.4-1 to the current 1.30.0-0, on amd64 and arm64 (50 packages), each against the checksum in the repository index. Each package installs one file, /sbom-indexer, as listed in the md5sums manifest of its control archive, and the MD5 checksum recorded there equals that of the program we read in full from the Alpine 3.23 package of the same version and architecture with the matching revision (for example 1.20.4-5 matches 1.20.4-r5 and 1.21.0-0 matches 1.21.0-r0; 1.26.0-3 matches the 1.26.0-r2 program, which 1.26.0-r3 also carries), so these packages carry the same statically linked Go programs, built with CGO_ENABLED=0 (no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies). The v1.2.1 tag is the fix commit itself and v1.2.2 contains it (GitHub compare). The program does not compile in sigstore-go's verifier: reading the Go function table of every build, with runtime.main and sigstore-go's own pkg/bundle package initialiser (pkg/bundle.init) found in every build as controls, shows that the only sigstore-go functions linked are the package initialisers of pkg/bundle and pkg/verify, alongside their package-level variables. sigstore-go's (*Verifier).Verify in pkg/verify, the only non-test function the fix changes, is not linked in any build, no function from pkg/root, where ExpiringKey is defined, is linked, and no ValidAtTime method is linked.
